haiku-low.q1: Both return the same 401 login page with the same body and headers. Unknown emails get a dummy bcrypt check so timing matches.
haiku-low.q2: The lock check runs first and returns 429 with Retry-After until locked_until. Nothing is written and the password is not checked.
haiku-low.q3: Its session row is deleted, because the server deletes the row matching the incoming cookie. The browser then gets a new token and new session.
haiku-low.q4: Only the raw random session ID, 32 base64url-encoded random bytes, in the __Host-session cookie. No user data. It is HttpOnly, so page scripts cannot read it.
haiku-low.q5: 12 hours after login. The absolute expiry is set once at login and never extended. Continuous use only restarts the 30-minute idle clock.
haiku-low.q6: It deletes the matching row if one exists, then redirects 302 to /login with a clear-cookie header. Expired, unknown and missing sessions look identical.
haiku-low.q7: The server deletes the session row for the token hash before responding. If the session is already gone, logout still redirects to /login with a cleared cookie.
haiku-low.q8: In the Postgres sessions table, shared by both instances. Any instance hashes the cookie token with SHA-256 and looks up that row, so no sticky sessions are needed.
haiku-low.q9: In the login_failures table, one row per failed attempt with email and failed_at. The server counts rows with failed_at within 10 minutes, counted back from each attempt.
haiku-low.q10: It checks that the token-hash row exists, last_seen_at is within 30 minutes and absolute_expires_at is after now. When valid, it writes last_seen_at as now and returns user_id.
haiku-low.q11: A 503 with a generic message and the cookie unchanged. The transaction rolls back, so the old session row is kept and no new session exists.
haiku-low.q12: A 10-minute timer in each app instance deletes expired session rows and old failure and lockout rows. Lookups reject expired rows anyway, so only table size is affected.

sonnet.q1: They do not differ: same status (401), body (login page: Invalid email or password) and headers; timing is matched by checking a dummy bcrypt hash.
sonnet.q2: It is rejected with a 429 login page (Too many attempts) with a Retry-After header, if the lock is active (locked_until after now). Nothing is written and the password is not checked. (The 5th failure itself returns 401 and sets a 15-minute lock; failure rows are deleted when the lock is set.)
sonnet.q3: On successful login the session row matching the incoming cookie is deleted (whatever it was), and a new session with a new token is created. On a failed login the old session stays valid and unchanged.
sonnet.q4: Only the raw random session ID (32 random bytes, base64url); no user data. The cookie is HttpOnly, so page JavaScript cannot read it.
sonnet.q5: At 12 hours after login (the absolute expiry, never extended), since constant use keeps resetting the 30-minute idle clock.
sonnet.q6: It deletes the row for that token hash if any, and responds with a 302 redirect to /login with a clear-cookie header (same as for a missing session).
sonnet.q7: If a cookie is present, the server deletes the session row for the token hash, then responds 302 to /login with a clear-cookie header. If there is no cookie (or no session), it gives the same 302 to /login with clear-cookie. If the delete fails with a database error, it returns 503 and keeps the cookie.
sonnet.q8: In the sessions table in the shared Postgres database. Either instance takes the cookie's token, hashes it with SHA-256 and looks up the row by token_hash in Postgres; no sticky sessions needed.
sonnet.q9: In the login_failures table in Postgres, one row per failed attempt (email, failed_at). The server counts rows for that email with failed_at in the last 10 minutes, using the database clock (now()), counted back from each attempt.
sonnet.q10: It runs an UPDATE on the sessions row matching the token hash where last_seen_at is within 30 minutes and absolute_expires_at is after now (database now()). If a row matches, it sets last_seen_at = now and returns user_id.
sonnet.q11: A database error before COMMIT rolls everything back and the browser gets a 503 with a generic message; the cookie is unchanged and the old session is kept.
sonnet.q12: A cleanup timer in each app instance, started at boot and running every 10 minutes, deletes sessions that are idle for 30 minutes or past absolute expiry (also old failure and lockout rows). Meanwhile lookups reject expired rows anyway.
